issues.description: The problem statement instructs students to store the result in a variable named `score_counter`, but the template repository does not declare any such variable and the solution repository declares a variable named `score_cnt` instead. This name mismatch (and the missing declaration in the template) creates confusion about the expected identifier and may cause students to fail automated checks or be penalized if the grader expects `score_counter`.
issues.suggestedFix: Ensure the variable name is consistent across all artifacts. Either (a) update the solution and template to declare and use `score_counter` (e.g. add `score_counter dd 0` in the data section and use that name), or (b) change the problem statement to require `score_cnt` if that name is preferred. Also add the declaration to the template so students have the expected symbol available.

issues.description: The problem statement asks students to store the result in a variable named `score_counter`, but the solution implementation declares `score_cnt` (and the template has no matching declaration). This naming mismatch across artifacts creates a mapping burden: students following the problem text will look for `score_counter` in the template/solution but find `score_cnt` (or nothing), causing unnecessary confusion about the expected identifier.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the variable in the solution to match the problem statement: replace `score_cnt dd 0` with `score_counter dd 0`. Also add the same declaration to the template (helloWorld.asm) in the .data section so students see the expected identifier in the starter code. Alternatively, update the problem statement to request `score_cnt` if that name is preferred, but keep names consistent across all artifacts.
